title: QWED Verification Context
description: QWED Verification Context v1.0 — the object of verification plus the context required to interpret, reproduce, and trust the verification. Derived from ADR-001..005.

spec_version.description: The specification version this document conforms to.

Verdict.description: The truth verdict (ADR-001, ADR-002). VERIFIED requires a proof_ref; UNVERIFIABLE and BLOCKED are fail-closed and carry no proof.

Admission.description: The safe-to-run decision (ADR-003). Separate from the truth verdict: truth != admission. Execution and shipping gate exclusively on admission == ADMIT.

ProofRef.description: An evidence commitment (ADR-002): sha256 of the canonical encoding of the bound payload. Provides evidence integrity and reproducibility. It is NOT itself the mathematical proof.

VerifiedObject.description: The object of verification (ADR-001): the formal statement being evaluated.

formal_statement.description: The formal statement being verified — the object of verification.

Formalization.description: The NL -> formal mapping (ADR-004). Exposed for confirmation but NEVER itself verified.

translator.description: The translator that produced the formal statement (untrusted, outside the trust boundary).

verified.description: The formalization is never verified (ADR-004). Always false.

VerificationContext.description: The Verification Context (ADR-002): everything required to interpret, reproduce, and trust the verification, in four layers.

Interpretation.description: The interpretation layer (ADR-001, ADR-002): required context that gives the object meaning. A statement is only a proposition relative to a theory. At least one interpretation field must be present.

theory.description: The theory / axiom set the statement is interpreted under.

logic.description: The logic the statement is expressed in.

dialect.description: The dialect (e.g. SQL dialect) where applicable.

parser_version.description: The parser version (e.g. SQL parser) where applicable.

language.description: The source language (e.g. for code verification) where applicable.

policy_version.description: The policy version (e.g. code security policy) where applicable.

algebra_domain.description: The algebra domain (e.g. real-closed field) where applicable.

Proof.description: The proof/discharge layer (ADR-002): the verifier is the trusted computing base. Declares how the object was discharged and how much to trust it.

verifier.description: The verifier / discharging engine (the trusted computing base).

configuration.description: Solver flags, timeouts, resource limits, and options that affect the outcome. Values MUST be within the canonical encoding's JSON domain.

theory_scope.description: The logic / axiom set / theory the discharge is relative to.

trusted_dependencies.description: Libraries and sub-components inside the trusted computing base.

outcome_treatment.description: How unknown/timeout/error outcomes are treated. These are never VERIFIED; they resolve to UNVERIFIABLE or BLOCKED (fail-closed).

Evidence.description: The evidence layer (ADR-002): what was checked, plus the evidence commitment.

evidence.description: The retained evidence the proof_ref commits to. Values MUST be within the canonical encoding's JSON domain; integers MUST be exactly representable as IEEE-754 doubles.

proof_ref.description: The evidence commitment. Non-null (sha256) iff verdict is VERIFIED; null for UNVERIFIABLE/BLOCKED.

Decision.description: The decision layer (ADR-003): the safe-to-run outcome. Truth != admission.

EncodableNumber.description: A JSON number within the canonical encoding's IEEE-754 domain. Integer values MUST be exactly representable as IEEE-754 doubles.

EncodableValue.description: A JSON value that can be canonicalized and bound by proof_ref.
